title: Best Lawn Care Business Software (2026 Prices)
description: Yardbook vs LawnPro vs QuoteIQ vs Jobber vs Service Autopilot vs LMN for lawn care: routing, chemical tracking and real prices, checked Oct 2026.
h1: Best lawn care business software for small crews
body:
Lawn care software has to handle three things well: recurring weekly or biweekly visits that generate themselves, routes that keep drive time down, and batch invoicing at the end of the week or month. Fertilizer and weed-control programs add a fourth: chemical application records. Below are six tools we could verify for lawn care businesses from each vendor's own pricing page, checked 2026-10-24 (LawnPro added 2026-10-26). Prices are as published; anything a vendor doesn't publish is marked unknown.

{{table:yardbook,lawnpro,quoteiq,jobber,service-autopilot,lmn}}

Quick price check for a solo operator

  • Yardbook Starter: free (a 1% Yardbook fee applies to online card payments on free accounts, on top of Stripe's fees).
  • LawnPro Solo: free for 1 user and up to 25 customers; Startup is $39/mo with unlimited customers.
  • QuoteIQ Essentials: $29.99/mo monthly, or $299.99/yr billed annually.
  • Jobber Core: $49/mo with no commitment, or $29/mo billed annually ($21/mo promo for the first 12 months on annual sign-ups before Oct 30, 2026).
  • Service Autopilot Startup: $49/mo (annual subscription rate; monthly rate not published).
  • LMN Starter: from $297/mo billed monthly, plus a one-time onboarding fee, but it includes 6 licenses.

1. Yardbook: the free starting point

Yardbook's Starter plan is free and covers customer management, jobs and scheduling, estimates, invoices, routing, expenses, reports, lot measurement, employee access, card payments, snow removal and a product catalog. Yardbook says the free plan is funded by sponsored ads. Business ($34.99/mo) adds bulk email and text (Twilio), GPS tracking, automatic backup, automatic invoice reminders, multi-step chemical programs and custom lead capture, and it waives the 1% Yardbook processing fee. Enterprise ($49.99/mo) adds QuickBooks sync, a branded company portal and no ads. Those prices are for annual plans. Yardbook says different rates apply month-to-month but doesn't publish them. The pricing page lists web, desktop and Android app access. See Yardbook pricing details.

2. QuoteIQ: measuring and quoting from the truck

QuoteIQ Essentials is $29.99/mo for 1 user and includes estimates (standard, options and package), invoices, invoice subscriptions, scheduling with recurring and multi-day jobs, online payments and customer financing through Stripe or Whop. For lawn work the useful extras start on Beginner ($99.99/mo, 2 users): MapMeasure Pro for measuring a property from the map, property lines, QuoteIQ Cam job photos, mass invoicing and expense tracking. Pro ($199.99/mo, 4 users) adds QuickBooks, job costing, text and email automation and chemical tracking, which QuoteIQ describes as pesticide application records, applicator licenses and exports for lawn and pest companies. Route optimization and online self-booking are on Elite ($299.99/mo, 10 users). Extra users are $25/mo each on every plan. Every plan has a 14-day trial, but a credit or debit card is needed to start, and there are no contracts or cancellation fees. Annual billing works out to 10 months' price for 12. {{aff:quoteiq|Try QuoteIQ free for 14 days}}

3. Jobber: recurring visits, batch invoicing and add-ons

Jobber's lawn care page lists automatically generated visits for recurring jobs, rescheduling after rain delays, route optimization, batch invoicing, automatic invoice reminders, quote templates and suggested add-ons such as edging, aeration, fertilization, mulching and seasonal cleanups. Core is $29/mo billed annually or $49/mo with no commitment, for 1 user; extra users are $29/mo each. On plan tiers: optional line items (upsells) on quotes start on Grow ($149/mo annually, $199/mo monthly), and automatic quote follow-ups and QuickBooks Online/Xero sync start on Connect ($99/mo annually, $139/mo monthly). Card payments are 2.9% + 30¢ online and ACH is 1%. The 14-day trial (on Grow) needs no credit card. Jobber's pricing page doesn't list chemical application tracking. {{aff:jobber|See Jobber plans}}

4. Service Autopilot: automations and snow, but annual pricing

Service Autopilot publishes annual subscription rates only: Startup $49/mo (1 business user, 1 mobile license), Pro $199/mo (2 mobile licenses), Pro Plus $499/mo (5 mobile licenses) and Elite on request (2 business users, 8 mobile licenses). Startup covers scheduling, dispatching, invoicing, payments, expense tracking and lead tracking. Route optimization, snow dispatch, chemical tracking, job costing and job proposals start on Pro. Automation workflows start on Pro Plus. QuickBooks Online two-way sync and two-way texting are included on Elite and listed as call-for-pricing on Pro and Pro Plus. No free trial is stated (the page offers demos), and downgrades take effect at the end of your contract period. See Service Autopilot pricing details.

5. LMN: for landscaping crews that estimate by the hour

LMN (by Granum) is built for landscape companies with crews. Starter is from $297/mo billed monthly and includes 1 office/crew lead license and 5 crew member licenses: budgeting with overhead recovery, estimating with material and labor calculators, scheduling, the LMN Crew app (route optimization, punch-ins, GPS verification, offline access), automated invoicing, LMN Pay (card, ACH, debit), a customer portal and QuickBooks Online. Professional is from $648/mo with 3 office and 15 crew licenses and adds real-time job costing, material tracking, subcontractor tracking and Zapier. Both prices come after a one-time onboarding fee that LMN doesn't publish, and extra licenses cost an unpublished fee. No free trial is stated. See LMN pricing details.

LawnPro: free to 25 customers, chemical programs on Grow

LawnPro is built for lawn care. Its Solo plan is free (1 user, up to 25 customers, no credit card) and includes scheduling, quotes, invoices with online payments, a client portal, time tracking at each job, level billing and service contracts, reporting and the mobile app. Startup ($39/mo, 3 employee logins) removes the customer cap and adds automated invoicing, online work requests, quote deposits, tips and bulk price updates. Grow ($129/mo, or $99/mo billed annually; 7 employee logins) adds optimized routes and route analytics, bulk scheduling, optional items on estimates, ACH payments, review-request automations and multi-step chemical programs. Plus ($249/mo, 15 employee logins) adds 2-way texting, auto-charging cards on file and QuickBooks Sync. LawnPro says annual billing saves 20% but only lists the annual price for Grow, and it doesn't publish add-on prices (QuickBooks Sync, routing on lower plans, DeepLawn AI measurements), card processing rates or trial length. No contracts; every paid plan has a free trial with no card needed. See LawnPro pricing details or the LawnPro pricing page.

Which should you pick?

  • Just starting, mowing a handful of yards: Yardbook Starter costs nothing. Once you take a steady stream of card payments online, compare the 1% fee against the $34.99/mo Business plan that waives it.
  • Want free software but have more than a few dozen yards: LawnPro Solo is free but caps you at 25 customers; Startup ($39/mo) removes the cap. Yardbook Starter doesn't state a customer limit.
  • Solo or two-person crew that quotes a lot of new properties: QuoteIQ Beginner ($99.99/mo, 2 users) adds map measuring and job photos. Jobber Core is cheaper at $29/mo annually, but its quote add-ons need Grow.
  • Fertilizer and weed-control programs: chemical tracking is on Yardbook (multi-step programs on Business), LawnPro Grow (multi-step chemical programs, $129/mo), QuoteIQ Pro and Service Autopilot Pro. LMN lists material tracking on Professional. Jobber's pricing page doesn't list it.
  • Crew of about five: LawnPro Grow includes 7 employee logins for $129/mo ($99/mo billed annually). QuoteIQ Pro (4 users) plus one $25 extra user comes to $224.99/mo. Jobber lists 5-user Connect at $149/mo and 5-user Grow at $229/mo, both billed annually. LMN Starter includes 6 licenses for $297/mo plus onboarding. Service Autopilot Pro Plus includes 5 mobile licenses for $499/mo (annual rate).
  • Lawn plus snow removal: Yardbook lists snow removal on the free plan, and Service Autopilot lists snow dispatch from Pro.

Pest and lawn operators who price by route can also look at GorillaDesk ($49/mo for 1 route, unlimited users). To price a mowing or cleanup job, try our free job quote estimator, and before you sign up anywhere, run through the software buying checklist. faq: What is the best free lawn care business software?

Of the tools we checked on 2026-10-24, Yardbook's Starter plan is free and includes scheduling, estimates, invoices, routing, card payments and snow removal. Yardbook charges a 1% fee on online payments for free and trial accounts, on top of Stripe's fees; the Business plan ($34.99/mo on an annual plan) waives it.
How much does lawn care software cost per month?

Published starting prices checked 2026-10-24 (LawnPro 2026-10-26): LawnPro free (Solo, up to 25 customers; Startup $39/mo), Yardbook free (paid plans $34.99 and $49.99/mo on annual plans), QuoteIQ $29.99/mo, Jobber $29/mo billed annually or $49/mo with no commitment, Service Autopilot $49/mo (annual subscription rate) and LMN from $297/mo billed monthly plus a one-time onboarding fee.
Which lawn care software tracks fertilizer and chemical applications?

Yardbook lists chemical tracking, with multi-step chemical programs on its Business plan. QuoteIQ lists chemical tracking (pesticide application records and applicator licenses) on Pro ($199.99/mo) and up. Service Autopilot lists chemical tracking on Pro ($199/mo) and up. LMN lists material tracking on Professional. Jobber's pricing page doesn't list chemical tracking. LawnPro lists multi-step chemical programs on Grow ($129/mo) and Plus.
Which lawn care apps have route optimization?

Yardbook lists routing on its free Starter plan. Service Autopilot lists route optimization on Pro and up. QuoteIQ lists route optimization on Elite ($299.99/mo) and Max. LMN lists route optimization in its LMN Crew app. Jobber lists route optimization on its lawn care page. LawnPro includes optimized routes on Grow ($129/mo) and Plus (add-on on Solo and Startup).
Do these lawn care tools sync with QuickBooks?

Jobber syncs with QuickBooks Online and Xero on Connect and up. QuoteIQ lists QuickBooks on Pro and up. Yardbook lists QuickBooks sync on Enterprise only. LMN lists QuickBooks Online on Starter and Online and Desktop on Professional. Service Autopilot includes QuickBooks Online two-way sync on Elite and lists it as call-for-pricing on Pro and Pro Plus.
